verdict.meaning: no cancellation below the challenge peak was found even with BKZ-40 at the real parameters, so the p-based margin survives the strongest reduction run here (upper bound only -- a larger block size could still do better)
verdict.why_reduction_changed_nothing: The naive basis row (-zeta*e_i, e_i) already achieves the minimum: its second block is a unit vector (norm 1) and its first block is a column of the circulant, whose entries are the challenge coefficients (norm p). Nothing shorter exists because any nonzero d forces at least one coefficient of magnitude >= 1 in the second block, and reducing the first block below p would require zeta to have smaller entries. So LLL/BKZ leaving row 0 untouched is the CORRECT outcome, not a failed reduction -- confirmed by the volume check and by verifying row 0 is a genuine cancellation.
